title: Home Was the Easy Part
author: GatorVault Staff
excerpt: Home was the easy part. Saturday is the first night that can decide whether 2-0 was a start or just two games that never got close.
takeaways: Florida is 2-0 because two home games never got close. Saturday is the first night that can decide whether that was a start.
The Campbell flags did not cost them at 45-3. The same flags, and the same slow start, can cost them at Auburn if the game is still close.
Sumrall's feeling after 52-3 is the story this week. Auburn is where that feeling gets measured.
Stop the run or you have no chance. Philo has been enough at home. Saturday is the first time the crowd is not his.
Honest range is still 7-5 or 8-4. Saturday would be the first 3-0 since 2019. Florida has not won at Auburn since 1999.

sources.reporter: Buster Faulkner and Brad White Tuesday

note: Hairline pass Sep 15, 2026. Not live. Await Charles approve.
body:
Florida is 2-0. That is what you are supposed to be after Florida Atlantic and Campbell. Both were at home. Neither game got close. That is why the record looks like a start, and why it is not a test. Home was the easy part. Saturday at Auburn is the first night Jon Sumrall's standard has to leave the Swamp.

They put 66 on Florida Atlantic because Aaron Philo went 16-of-21 for 275 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception, Jadan Baugh ran 14 times for 160 and three, and neither one had to do it against a team that could get close. Vernell Brown III caught six for 117. Eric Singleton Jr. left on an ankle. A building will take 66-21 and call itself ready. Sumrall spent the next Monday watching the snaps that would not survive a building that is not theirs.

What he saw on that tape was football IQ: knowing what the play is asking, the down and distance, when they speed it up, when to crowd a receiver and when to give him space. On 3rd-and-short a corner sat nine yards off the ball, which is too far. They took away the long passes and let FAU speed the game up. The interception was a catchable ball, not on Philo. Philo changed the play at the line when he needed to, and led. The win was real. The tape was the first sign that 2-0 could still be a disguise.

Campbell was the next home Saturday, and the first series made that sign public. Completions down the field, then a field goal, the kind of start Sumrall told the defensive backs not to get scared of. At corner you are going to get beat. Next play. If that opening lives at Auburn while the score is still a score, home has already run out.

What followed was home doing what home has done, which is the problem. By the time Baugh scored from the 2 it was 45-3, built on Philo's run from the 3, Patrick Durkin's 28-yard field goal, Vernell Brown III twice on returns and once from 14, and Dallas Wilson's 40, with Philo at 242 yards and two scores. That is what a night looks like when the other team cannot stay in it, and it still cannot tell you Saturday.

Once it was 45-3, the night could afford a second half. Saturday will not. Sumrall put the backups in and the flags came with them. T.J. Shanahan Jr. on back-to-back snaps, a hold that wiped a Baugh run that was already a big gain, then a personal foul. Roderick Kearney picked up another. That is 1st-and-25, and in this league the drive is already over. Seven flags after halftime. One in the first half. Three in the whole opener. Up 45-3 those flags do not change the score. If they show up when the game is still close, they are how you lose, and that is the version of this team Byrum Brown and Jeremiah Cobb will actually get to play.

The 75 late in the third was leftover from a night that had already been decided, the only kind of night that can absorb seven flags. Last year Baugh's longest was 26 yards. In two weeks he has 296 yards and five scores on 14 carries each Saturday. Campbell stayed on three. The Swamp left with 52-3 and a 2-0 start it had not had in five years, the number you get when nobody can get close.

Sumrall walked to the locker room unhappy with that number in his pocket on a night most new coaches would have taken. Happy they got the win. Not pleased with a lot of the rest. Second-team and third-team guys got a chance to prove people right or wrong, and some of them showed why they are not playing. Sumrall called the depth behind Baugh subpar. A guy went the wrong way on one run. Somebody missed a protection call. The starting offensive line was not awful and is not where it needs to be. They did not give Baugh as many rushing lanes as they should have. Year One in this building is a coach deciding, in public, that 52-3 is not the point. Freshmen have been here since January. Play that second half in conference and they are about to have a real rude awakening. Walk in like that and they will get absolutely embarrassed.

Monday, that feeling still had Auburn on it. It had cooled, and it had not left. The depth had not played clean, and the team that will punish that is already in Jordan-Hare. Sumrall wants them to finish on the quarterback. He wants sacks. These games count twice, he said, overall record and conference record, and the last two weeks counted once. If he has to get anybody ready to play SEC football, they have the wrong people here. Jeremiah Cobb and Omar Mabson II are both over 5.5 yards a carry and have 265 combined. Byrum Brown ran for a thousand yards and 14 scores last year, physical, playing with confidence, a lot of time in this system. The spacing and the shots get everybody's attention. What kills you is the run. If you do not stop it, you have no chance. Home let Florida pick the terms, and Auburn is not built to hand them back.

They may also walk into that without Singleton and Oyebadejo. Both are out of the boot, both were very limited Monday, both questionable, and Sumrall will not promise either one plays. Philo is the piece that has not had to prove anything away from here. He is confident and not easily rattled. If he plays like he has played through the first part of this year, Sumrall said, he will give them a chance to win every week. That has been enough with this crowd behind him. It has to be enough in a building that will not help him.

If that Saturday is as close as Sumrall thinks it can be, Tuesday belonged to the two men who have to call it. Buster Faulkner has to take a quarterback who has only started at home and keep him clean when DJ Durkin's defense is playing with its hair on fire, fast and confident. Same preparation every week, no matter who they play. You are not just playing 11 defenders. You have the crowd. Faulkner said Philo is cool, calm, and collected. They will coach him through it.

If Faulkner has to keep Philo clean, Brad White has to keep the other side of that close game from becoming a track meet. He has to take a defense that just spent two weeks in the Swamp and put it in a fight that already knows its own offense. Auburn has been in Alex Golesh's system for years. Pace, tempo, skill, a nasty offensive line. Fist fight. Rock fight. Be ready for that.

Florida scored 118 and allowed 24 at home. Auburn does not play those two games, and the card after that is why a close one this week is not just Week 3. Florida has not won at Auburn since 1999. Ole Miss, Missouri, South Carolina, Texas in Austin, and Georgia in Atlanta on Halloween are still waiting. Two home blowouts do not change those. The honest range for this roster is still 7-5 or 8-4. First 3-0 since 2019 is what Saturday would be.

Home was the easy part. Saturday is the first night that can decide whether 2-0 was a start or just two games that never got close.
